repositories.citation: [1] Model Context Protocol. 'TypeScript SDK - Official TypeScript SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients.' GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk
repositories.architecture: SDK provides transport abstraction layer with pluggable transports (STDIO, StreamableHTTP). StreamableHTTPServerTransport handles HTTP POST/GET/DELETE requests, manages SSE streams, and coordinates session lifecycle.

import { StreamableHTTPServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/streamableHttp.js';
const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: () => randomUUID() });

InMemoryEventStore not suitable for distributed deployments

repositories.citation: [2] Model Context Protocol. 'Official MCP Servers - Everything Example with StreamableHTTP.' GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/everything/streamableHttp.ts

alternatives: Redis-backed session storage for distributed deployment

repositories.citation: [6] bh-rat. 'mcp-db - Session and event store for MCP server, also allows distributed coordination between servers.' GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/bh-rat/mcp-db

repositories.architecture: Intercepts MCP StreamableHTTP traffic at transport level. Persists sessions as JSON in Redis. Events stored in Redis Streams with sequential IDs. Any node can reconstruct SDK transport from stored session data, enabling true horizontal scaling without sticky sessions.

repositories.citation: [8] Model Context Protocol. 'Transports - Model Context Protocol Specification 2025-03-26.' Official Documentation, 2025. https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports
repositories.architecture: Unified endpoint design replacing previous dual-channel (HTTP + SSE) approach. Server MAY assign session IDs at initialization. Clients MUST include session IDs on subsequent requests if provided. Server MUST send each message on only one SSE stream when multiple connections exist.

key_code_patterns.session_storage: const transports: Map<string, StreamableHTTPServerTransport> = new Map();
key_code_patterns.initialization: transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: () => randomUUID(), eventStore, onsessioninitialized: (sessionId) => { transports.set(sessionId, transport); } });
key_code_patterns.cleanup: server.onclose = async () => { const sid = transport.sessionId; if (sid && transports.has(sid)) { transports.delete(sid); await cleanup(); } };
key_code_patterns.graceful_shutdown: process.on('SIGINT', async () => { for (const [sessionId, transport] of transports) { await transport.close(); transports.delete(sessionId); } process.exit(0); });

health_check_patterns.basic_liveness: app.get('/health', (req, res) => { res.status(200).json({ status: 'healthy', timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), service: 'mcp-server', uptime: process.uptime() }); });
health_check_patterns.readiness_with_dependencies: app.get('/health/ready', async (req, res) => { const mcpReady = mcpServer.isInitialized && mcpServer.tools.length > 0; const dbConnected = await checkDatabaseConnection(); const ready = mcpReady && dbConnected; res.status(ready ? 200 : 503).json({ ready, checks: { mcp: mcpReady, database: dbConnected } }); });
health_check_patterns.prometheus_metrics: app.get('/metrics', (req, res) => { const metrics = [ `mcp_server_up ${healthState.isReady ? 1 : 0}`, `mcp_server_uptime_seconds ${process.uptime()}`, `mcp_tools_total ${mcpServer.tools?.length || 0}`, `mcp_active_sessions ${transports.size}` ]; res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain'); res.send(metrics.join('\n')); });
health_check_patterns.caching_strategy: const HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT = 5000; const DEPENDENCY_CHECK_INTERVAL = 30000; // Cache dependency checks for 30 seconds to prevent overload

implementation_recommendations.rationale: Current stdio-server.ts works perfectly for local development. No need for HTTP complexity. Single process per agent. Easy debugging. No network configuration required.
implementation_recommendations.implementation_notes: Keep existing STDIO transport. Use Claude Desktop with stdio transport config. No changes needed to current architecture.

implementation_recommendations.rationale: Simple stateless deployment. Each request independent. Easy to scale horizontally. No session management complexity. Works with any load balancer. Can deploy to Kubernetes, ECS, or VM.
implementation_recommendations.implementation_notes: Add Express server with POST /mcp endpoint. Use sessionIdGenerator: undefined. Store any needed state in database per request. Simple deployment with no sticky sessions needed.

implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: StreamableHTTP with stateful mode + in-memory sessions + sticky sessions
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Need conversation context per agent. Can use in-memory Map for session storage. Deploy behind ALB/Nginx with sticky sessions. Sessions survive for duration of agent conversation. Supports SSE for notifications.
implementation_recommendations.implementation_notes: Use official reference implementation pattern (everything/streamableHttp.ts). Configure ALB with cookie-based routing. Monitor memory usage per session. Implement session timeout (e.g., 1 hour). Add health checks for orchestration.

implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: StreamableHTTP with stateful mode + Redis session storage
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Need distributed session storage for horizontal scaling. Redis enables session failover across nodes. No sticky sessions required. Can scale to thousands of agents. High availability with Redis cluster. Sessions survive node restarts.
implementation_recommendations.implementation_notes: Implement custom Redis-backed session store (no SDK support yet - requires custom code). Store session state and event log in Redis. Use Redis Streams for event replay. Deploy multiple server instances behind standard load balancer. Implement session serialization/deserialization. Reference mcp-db project for patterns (Python), adapt to TypeScript.
implementation_recommendations.current_limitation: No official TypeScript SDK support for Redis persistence yet. Need custom implementation. mcp-db (Python) shows pattern but is experimental.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Serverless Deployment (AWS Lambda, Vercel, Cloud Functions)
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Lambda doesn't support long-lived connections. Stateless mode perfect for serverless. Each invocation independent. Scale to zero when idle. Pay per request. Simple deployment model.
implementation_recommendations.implementation_notes: Use sessionIdGenerator: undefined. Store any needed state in DynamoDB/Firestore. Keep functions warm with scheduled pings. Set appropriate timeout (30s max for Lambda). No SSE support in serverless. Use JSON responses only.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Hybrid Development + Production (Recommended for Midnight MCP)
implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: Support both STDIO and StreamableHTTP transports with shared service layer
implementation_recommendations.rationale: STDIO for development (Claude Desktop, local testing). StreamableHTTP for production (multi-agent deployment). Shared MCPServer and service layer. Transport is swappable. Single codebase for both modes.
implementation_recommendations.implementation_notes: Keep existing stdio-server.ts for development. Add new http-server.ts for production. Both use same MCPServer class and ServiceDependencies. Environment variable to choose transport (TRANSPORT=stdio|http). WalletOrchestrator remains unchanged. Services layer unchanged.

kubernetes.deployment:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: midnight-mcp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: midnight-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: midnight-mcp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mcp-server
        image: midnight-mcp:latest
        env:
        - name: TRANSPORT
          value: http
        - name: PORT
          value: "3000"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 30
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/ready
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 2Gi
            cpu: 1000m
          requests:
            memory: 1Gi
            cpu: 500m
kubernetes.service:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: midnight-mcp
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: midnight-mcp
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
  sessionAffinity: ClientIP # For stateful sessions without Redis
kubernetes.hpa:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: midnight-mcp-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: midnight-mcp
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70

docker_compose.compose:
version: '3.8'
services:
  mcp-server:
    build: .
    environment:
      - TRANSPORT=http
      - PORT=3000
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    depends_on:
      - redis
    restart: unless-stopped
  
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  redis-data:

aws_lambda.serverless_config:
service: midnight-mcp
provider:
  name: aws
  runtime: nodejs20.x
  timeout: 30
  environment:
    TRANSPORT: http
functions:
  mcp:
    handler: dist/lambda.handler
    events:
      - http:
          path: /mcp
          method: post
          cors: true

key_findings: StreamableHTTP is the recommended transport for production multi-agent MCP servers
Official TypeScript SDK provides StreamableHTTPServerTransport with full session management
Three deployment modes: stateless (serverless), stateful with sticky sessions (small-medium scale), stateful with Redis (large scale 100+)
Midnight MCP current architecture (STDIO) works perfectly for development, needs HTTP transport for production
Existing MCPServer and service layer can be reused unchanged - only transport layer needs to change
Phase 1 (stateless POC) can be done in 4-8 hours to validate approach
Phase 2 (stateful sessions) adds 8-16 hours for production-ready multi-agent support
Redis-backed scaling (Phase 4) requires 40-60 hours and custom implementation (no SDK support)
Recommended approach: hybrid architecture supporting both STDIO (dev) and HTTP (prod) from same codebase
summary.recommended_action: Start with Phase 1 (stateless POC) to validate StreamableHTTP integration with Midnight MCP architecture, then proceed to Phase 2 (stateful sessions) for production deployment supporting 10-50 concurrent agents. Defer Phase 4 (Redis) until actually needed (50+ agents).
immediate_next_steps: Validate tool calls work over HTTP
